turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, I came in because I keep losing these big chunks of time lately. 

I just... I find myself constantly re-reading emails and texts, or reopening folders on my computer. And it's not just at work. Before I even leave the house or start my day, I end up mentally replaying conversations over and over in my head. It’s like I’m trying to prove to myself that I didn’t make some kind of serious mistake. It's just really starting to get in the way of things.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes repetitive checking behaviors (re-reading emails, reopening folders) and mental rituals (replaying conversations) to prevent or verify they didn't make a mistake, which directly reflects compulsions.

turns.doctor_question: When you re-read or replay things, does it feel driven by a strong doubt that you may have made a serious mistake even when you know it probably isn’t true?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, that's exactly what it is. It's this intense doubt. Even when I’m trying to focus on my job—like if I'm working through a system design or preparing a lesson—this thought just keeps barging in. 

I'll suddenly get worried that I sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or that I somehow mishandled some family photos, or let someone in the community down. And... I know I’ve been over it already. I know in my head it's fine, but I just can’t seem to let it pass.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient explicitly confirms experiencing persistent, intrusive, and unwanted doubts and worries that barge into their thoughts and cannot be dismissed despite knowing rationally that they are fine.

turns.doctor_question: Do these doubts and the urge to check or replay things feel intrusive and unwanted to you?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, very much so. I mean... I definitely don't want to be having these thoughts. They just force their way in, even when I'm right in the middle of writing some code or doing something completely unrelated. 

It's frustrating because I really just want to move on with my day, but... I feel stuck until I go back and check or rethink the whole thing. So, yes, they are definitely unwanted.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient confirms experiencing intrusive and unwanted thoughts that force their way into consciousness even when engaged in unrelated activities.

turns.doctor_question: When you go back to re-read or mentally replay things, does doing that temporarily relieve your anxiety?

I'm... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really noticed if it actually makes me feel better. 

I just... I know I feel stuck until I do it, but I don't know if I'd call it relief afterward. I just haven't really thought about it that way. I just do it because I feel like I have to.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel driven to repeat these checking or mental review routines, even when you know they probably aren’t necessary?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, definitely. That's actually the main reason I came in to see someone. I... I keep losing chunks of time doing exactly that. 

I'll be getting ready to leave the house or about to start work, and I just get stuck re-reading emails and texts, or reopening the same folders on my computer over and over. symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly confirms feeling driven to perform repetitive checking behaviors (re-reading messages, reopening folders) and mental acts (mentally replaying conversations) despite knowing they are not necessary.

turns.doctor_question: Do these thoughts usually feel like ongoing worry about real-life problems in your life, rather than a need to check because something might be wrong?
